jobs.title: Chief Executive Officer Mental Health Superintendent 1 | Office/On-site #260908-5701MP-001
jobs.description:
Introduction

THE POSITION

The State of Connecticut , Department of Mental Health and Addiction Services (DMHAS) is seeking a mission-driven and experienced individual to lead as the Chief Executive Officer (Mental Health Superintendent 1)
of Capitol Region Mental Health Center (CRMHC), a state operated Local Mental Health Authority (LMHA). This role is responsible for the executive management of direct service programs within the Greater Hartford area.

The CEO will guide CRMHC's clinical and administrative operations, foster a culture of recovery and wellness, and ensure the delivery of high-quality, patient-centered care. The ideal candidate will have experience leading complex behavioral health programs, along with demonstrated strengths in financial stewardship, quality improvement, and workforce development.

CRMHC is a community based mental health center operated by DMHAS, providing a broad range of innovative clinical and community support services to individuals with psychiatric disabilities, often with co-occurring substance use disorders. CRMHC serves more than 1,800 clients annually and operates with a unionized staff of over 200. Services include a sixteen bed hospital level of care, Mobile Crisis, Assertive Community Team, Young Adult Services, Forensics and Jail Diversion, Deaf & Hard of Hearing, Peer Supports, Community Supports and Behavioral Home Health. Additionally, CRMHC has ties to 18 affiliate organizations serving approximately 3,000 clients, as well as memorandums of understanding with the City of Hartford and UConn.

HIGHLIGHTS

DIVISION: Capitol Region Mental Health Center (CRMHC)
LOCATION: Hartford, CT
SCHEDULE: Full-Time, 40 hours per week, First Shift, Monday through Friday
POSITION NUMBER: 25740

What We Can Offer You

Visit our new State Employee Benefits Overview page!
Professional growth and development opportunities
A healthy work/life balance to all employees

In This Role, You Will

Lead and Supervise: Provide oversight and guidance of Capitol Region Mental Health Center, as well as the clinical and administrative leadership team. Monitor facility service utilization data to confirm compliance with required standards and timely expectations of services to be delivered, develop and adhere to productivity expectations of all services.
Ensure Quality Care: Ensure that the Greater Hartford area population and DMHAS target populations receive appropriate and effective services. Develop and secure development and compliance of systemic performance standards.
Implement Policy & Standards: Put Agency program, policies and mission into practice within the Network. Facilitate the development of performance standards for private non-profit agencies and monitor service utilization data to confirm compliance with required standards.
Foster Collaboration: Build and maintain strong partnerships across areas and engage with local advisory groups, behavioral health organizations, advocacy groups, and consumer action teams.
Manage Operations: Oversee compliance with bargaining unit contracts. Prepare annual operating plan and ensure efficient and effective operations to maintain fidelity to the Network’s budget, timeliness of services rendered, adherence to mission centric community expectations.
Workforce Planning: Lead workforce strategies that prioritize client and family involvement in service delivery and decision-making, developing clinically trained staffing, effective and efficient strategies for productivity measures, create team decision-making for sound clinical outcomes.
Continuous Improvement: Identify and address service gaps through strategic planning and implementation, program monitoring, corrective action plans, performance improvement plans, and adherence to Office of the Commissioner’s strategic goals and objectives.
Consumer Advocacy: Implement the DMHAS grievance process to ensure timely and appropriate resolution of concerns raised by clients, families, and agencies.

About Us

DMHAS is a health care agency whose mission is to promote the overall health and wellness of persons with behavioral health needs through an integrated network of holistic, comprehensive, effective, and efficient services and supports that foster dignity, respect, and self-sufficiency in those we serve.

A comprehensive medical examination, including a drug screening, will be required of all applicants upon a conditional offer of employment.
All state employees must adhere to Connecticut's Policy for a Drug Free Workplace .

PURPOSE OF JOB CLASS (NATURE OF WORK)

In the Department of Mental Health and Addiction Services this class is accountable for developing and directing the clinical and administrative programs and operations of a mental health facility, hospital or community mental health center.

EXAMPLES OF DUTIES

Plans, develops and directs clinical and administrative program at a mental health facility, hospital or community based mental health center in accordance with policies established by the governing body;
Participates in planning and development of regional mental health service systems;
Participates in policy and subcommittee meetings;
Presides at administrative conferences with department heads to formulate policies to meet regional needs;
Develops and monitors programs;
Establishes and monitors procedures for facility;
Confers with visitors, relatives, and professional consultants regarding patients and clients and agency practices;
Ensures conformance of all facility procedures and programs with relevant statues and regulations;
Directs preparation and management of budget in conjunction with department heads;
Assures continued facility accreditation by Joint Commission on the Accreditation of Hospitals;
Leads the recruitment and hiring of staff, including outreach, interview and selection;
Performs related duties as required.

KNOWLEDGE, SKILL AND ABILITY

Considerable knowledge of
and ability to apply management principles and practices;
relevant state and federal laws, statutes, and regulations;
behavioral health policies and systems;
principles and practices of public and/or health care administration;
managed health care systems;
mental health program planning and development;

Knowledge of quality assessment and/or improvement techniques and accreditation body standards;
Considerable
interpersonal skills;
oral and written communication skills;

Considerable ability to collaborate within department, state, community, and agency constituent groups;
Ability to analyze fiscal data and prepare budgets.

Minimum Qualifications - General Experience

A Master's degree or higher in a health related field and at least six (6) years of managerial experience in hospital, health or mental health administration.

Preferred Qualifications

Current licensure as a clinical social worker, professional counselor, marital and family therapist, or clinical psychologist.
Experience overseeing compliance and privacy responsibilities of a healthcare agency.
Experience working within a senior management team, overseeing multidisciplinary teams of staff and departments.
Experience leading and implementing the mission & vision of a healthcare organization.
Experience in a management capacity directing programs and operations of behavioral health or health care services.
Experience in data analysis of services

jobs.title: Director of Operations - Texas State University Dining
jobs.description:
Job Description

As a Director of Operations you will plan, manage, and guide contracted services for multiple sites for a client or for multiple clients normally generating $2-15M+ in revenue to meet operating and financial goals, client objectives, and customer needs.

Depending on the client(s), services can include food service, facility support, custodial services, retail, lodging, transportation, and more. Our Dirctor of Operations are capable operations managers who lead a team to provide excellent service to our clients. With knowledge of the client's business, positive relationship building skills, financial savvy, and a focus on safety, our team makes a difference every day.

Job Responsibilities

The Successful Director Of Operations:

Leads a team that provides operational expertise in contracted services while providing hands-on execution management of operations.
Manages the client and community relationships at the location, continually assessing operations, and developing plans to provide optimal service and drive employee and customer satisfaction.
Builds, develops, and leads a management team and staff capable of carrying out organizational objectives.
Recommends methods, resources, and implementation for service improvement and growth based on understanding of operational needs, capabilities, & contractual obligations.
In partnership with Finance, manages a budget and assists in the design of improvements to optimize financial performance and operational productivity.
Manages compliance with all local, state and federal regulations and codes and maintains all associated records and reports.
Ensures compliance with Aramark's standards of operation including safety standards and Aramark's Business Conduct Policy at all times.

Qualifications

In order to be prepared for this leadership role, qualified candidates will possess:

Bachelor's degree level education highly preferred in an area of Food Service, Hospitality, Facilities, or Business Management.
The ability to focus on client and customer services, entrepreneurship and building and growing a strong business is essential to success in this role.
Savvy interpersonal skills to communicate effectively with clients, senior management, and Aramark support staff.
Comfortable reading, understanding, and implementing contractual requirements, including identifying opportunities within contract terms and conditions to address operational issues.
Meaningful experience in service industry, contract services, or hospitality environment.
Proven ability leading through other managers.
Experience in creating and managing a department budget, financial controls and analysis.
Experience crafting product sales strategies and implementing operational programs and initiatives.

This role may have physical demands including, but not limited to, lifting, bending, pushing, pulling and/or extended walking and standing. This role may also require uniforms and/or usage of Personal Protective Equipment (PPE).

Our Mission

Rooted in service and united by our purpose, we strive to do great things for each other, our partners, our communities, and our planet.

At Aramark, we believe that every employee should enjoy equal employment opportunity and be free to participate in all aspects of the company. jobs.title: Director of Communications & Public Engagement
jobs.description:
Position Overview

This position is a 1.0 FTE appointment serving the School Architecture and Design at the University of Kansas.

Working in collaboration with the Dean and the leadership team of the School, the position oversees all communications and marketing initiatives for the School and its units to translate complex students, alumni, faculty and staff achievements and impacts into clear, compelling narratives that improve student enrollment, retention, engagement and success; support advancement and fundraising; and promote reputation and community excellence.

The position is a member of the Dean’s leadership team. The position liaises with KU Marketing and Public Affairs, and KU Endowment Association on matters related to communications and public engagement. The position supervises the Graphic Designer of the School and a staff of student employees. The Position serves at the pleasure of the Dean and reports to the Dean.

Job Description

Responsibilities Related to Strategic Communications (90%)

Strategic Leadership Responsibilities

Works with the Dean and the leadership team of the School to develop and implement an integrated strategic communications plan to advance the School’s brand and increase awareness of its programs, activities, and mission. The plan will identify priority audiences, messages, channels, responsibilities, an editorial schedule, and measures of success.
Works directly and regularly with Department Chairs to understand departmental priorities, upcoming initiatives, events, accomplishments, recruitment needs, and opportunities for communication and promotion. Meets with the Chairs collectively or individually at least four times each academic year( twice per semester) to maintain consistent communication between the departments and the School’s communications efforts.
Provides editorial direction and brand management to enhance School brand and reputation.
Provides oversight of the School’s marketing and communications materials. Establishes and manages a process for review and feedback on visual communications, actively seeking input from School leadership to help ensure materials appropriately represent the School and its programs.
Develops a communications strategy for increasing the visibility of faculty research, scholarship, and creative activity across Architecture & Design, identifying opportunities to promote faculty expertise and accomplishments to academic, professional, industry, media, alumni, donor, and public audiences.

Day-to-day management responsibilities:

Maintains a clear editorial and project process for intake, prioritization, approvals, production, status updates, publication, and follow-up across web, social media, email, print, media relations, and events.
Builds and executes systematic and sustainable processes for documenting School outputs, events, lectures, faculty and student research, and activities with alumni, community and industry.
Maintains an active presence across the School and regularly engages with faculty and students to develop a strong understanding of the School’s programs, people, activities, accomplishments, and culture. Identifies stories and communications opportunities through direct engagement with the School community rather than relying solely on submitted content.
Attends key School events, Annual Board Meetings, lectures, exhibitions, reviews, student activities, and other activities as appropriate to identify and capture stories, moments, quotes, achievements, and other content for use across School communications.
Meets regularly with faculty across Architecture and Design to learn about their current and emerging research, scholarship, creative activity, publications, exhibitions, awards, grants, collaborations, and areas of expertise. Proactively identifies opportunities to translate and promote this work through School communications rather than relying solely on faculty to submit stories or requests.
Coordinates photography and other documentation of student work, faculty activities, events, exhibitions, facilities, and the everyday life of the School, working with professional photographers, student employees, faculty, and staff as appropriate.
Builds and executes systematic and sustainable processes for managing assets for public communications that strategically and creatively promote the past, present and future of the School.
Establishes a sustainable, repeatable and effective way for faculty, staff and students to submit requests, understand priorities, know who approves the work, and see what is moving forward.
Maintains the School website as a current and accurate representation of its programs, people, student work, research, activities, and accomplishments. Establishes a schedule for ongoing updates and an annual refresh of student work, photography, program information, and editorial content so that the website remains timely, relevant, and visually engaging.

Production Responsibilities

Manages the School’s websites and webpages including maintaining current content, improving navigation and usability, and ensuring information is accurate and accessible.
Manages the production of marketing and recruitment collateral materials of the School in collaboration with the Director of Recruitment and Enrollment and the Chairs, highlighting the Return on Investment (ROI) of a specific academic program through career outcomes, salary data, and alumni success; student experience; and innovation and research.
Manages the production of weekly newsletters for students and faculty in collaboration with the Director of Student Services and Success and the Chairs, highlighting weekly events and activities, policy updates, programmatic changes, and School resources to improve internal community engagement, inclusivity, and belonging.
Manages the production of the bi-monthly ArcD Newsletter highlighting student, faculty and alumni achievements and stories to improve engagement within the broader School community, including alumni, donors, and industry and community partners.
Manages the semiannual or annual publication/s of the School focusing on research, community, and economic impacts of the School for regional, national and international audiences.
Develops and produces ongoing stories and content that make faculty research, scholarship, creative activity, and expertise accessible and visible to audiences through the website, newsletters, social media, publications, media outreach, and other appropriate channels.

Public Engagement Responsibilities

Develops and promotes a unified ecosystem of public engagement for the School. Such an ecosystem will have multiple points of entry for both internal and external constituents to the creative and research output, community-engaged activities, events and workshops, services, and everyday life of the School; and will use the digital, physical, spatial and human assets of the School.
Builds relationships with faculty and students across Architecture and Design to ensure that communications reflect the breadth of the School and that emerging work, accomplishments, research, creative activity, and student experiences are identified and communicated.
Actively promotes faculty research and expertise.
Develops and stores collections and coordinates services that enhance communications and engagement activities through exhibitions, displays and other public efforts.
Promotes a positive and cooperative team environment among all stakeholder groups.
Pitches faculty experts to journalists for commentary on breaking news to elevate the unit's national profile.

Supervisory and Other Responsibilities (10%)

Supervises the Graphic Designer of the School and a staff of student employees.
Develops guidelines to distinguish the director’s strategy, priority-setting, and approval responsibilities from the designer’s creative and production responsibilities.
Establishes clear expectations and review processes for the quality and consistency of visual communications produced by the School. Actively seeks design expertise and feedback to help establish and maintain the visual direction of the School, ensuring that communications reflect the quality and standards of a School of Architecture and Design.
Develops clear expectations for staff development, workload priorities, coverage, delegation, and consistent service to the members of the School community.
Serves on committees, as needed.
Participates in and provides communications support for School activities including Board meetings, alumni events and award ceremonies, donor events, lecture series, and exhibitions.
Performs other duties in support of the mission of the School.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s Degree in Journalism, Communications, Marketing, Business Administration or a related field and five years of related experience
Previous experience with editing, writing and website maintenance
At least one year of supervisory experience
Prior work experience working with a wide range of populations, as demonstrated by application materials and work history

This position requires a formal degree in the cited discipline area(s) to ensure that candidates have advanced knowledge, analytical skills and professional competencies necessary to perform the duties of the position. The level of degree is commonly recognized as the standard qualification for similar roles in the public and private sector, ensuring that the university remains competitive with industry aligned practices, enhances collaboration with external partners, and supports the delivery of services and programs that meet professional and market-driven expectations.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with AI technologies for predictive analytics and yield modeling; personalized campaigns; and for administrative automation and document processing
Excellent computer skills and demonstrated interest and capacity in database management
Experience collaborating with different levels of leadership, including university and school leaderships as demonstrated by application materials and work history
Experience with strategic communications
Knowledge of developing surveys and analyzing data for reporting purposes
Proven experience exercising initiatives, decision-making and self-discipline
Experience in all or some of the other areas of responsibilities of the position
Demonstrated effective written communication skills as evidenced by application materials
Demonstrated organizational skills and demonstrated ability to handle multiple projects and juggle priorities

Additional Candidate Instructions

A Complete Application Consists Of

cover letter
resume
list of three professional references

Application review begins Friday, October 9, 2026. To ensure consideration please apply prior to this date.

Contact Information to Applicants

Jim Hammen

jhammen@ku.edu

Advertised Salary Range

$62,000 - $72,000, commensurate with experience

Application Review Begins

Friday October 9, 2026

Anticipated Start Date

Monday November 2, 2026

jobs.title: Executive Director, Trade Relations
jobs.description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Executive Director, Trade Relations based in United States.

This senior leadership role owns trade and patient-support strategy in preparation for the commercial launch of an innovative pharmaceutical product.

Reporting to the SVP of Market Access, you will define enterprise-wide approaches across distribution, GPOs, patient support programs, and strategic partners.

The position serves as a critical connection point between commercial strategy and operational execution, ensuring channels and partners are launch-ready.

You will work closely with Finance, Marketing, Legal, Compliance, Commercial Operations, Supply Chain, Regulatory, and Market Access teams to establish effective trade operations.

The role combines strategic planning, complex contract negotiations, organizational leadership, operational problem-solving, and performance management.

You will also establish governance frameworks that support compliant, consistent, and high-quality patient services while optimizing access and product availability.

This is a remote executive opportunity with significant external engagement and 50%+ travel, including regular travel to Boston.

Accountabilities

Lead product launch readiness by gathering, evaluating, and integrating critical trade, distribution, and patient-support requirements.
Design and execute comprehensive trade and patient-support strategies that strengthen market access and improve the overall patient experience.
Develop and implement GPO contracting strategies aligned with market access priorities and commercial objectives.
Build and lead a high-performing organization spanning trade operations, patient support, and field reimbursement.
Lead strategic negotiations with specialty distributors, specialty pharmacies, GPOs, patient hubs, and other key channel partners.
Serve as the primary subject-matter expert for trade operations, providing internal teams with relevant channel insights, guidance, and strategic direction.
Identify operational risks, inefficiencies, and opportunities, developing foundational and innovative solutions that improve efficiency, profitability, and product availability.
Monitor competitive and market dynamics to anticipate challenges, inform strategic decisions, and identify emerging opportunities.
Establish and maintain patient-support policies, business rules, governance structures, and operating frameworks that promote compliant and consistent service delivery.
Build and maintain trusted relationships with strategic external partners to strengthen collaboration and long-term value.
Ensure trade and patient-support initiatives are delivered against budgets, forecasts, operational objectives, and broader corporate performance targets.
Drive cross-functional alignment across commercial, operational, regulatory, financial, legal, and compliance stakeholders to ensure coordinated execution.

Requirements

Bachelor’s degree in a relevant field; an MBA is preferred.
12+ years of experience across pharmaceutical trade, distribution, GPOs, patient support, and strategic partner management.
Demonstrated pharmaceutical trade and patient-support experience supporting the launch of a new product.
Experience developing and implementing channel strategies in complex pharmaceutical environments.
Experience negotiating, implementing, executing, and monitoring contracts with channel partners.
Experience with specialty distributors, specialty pharmacies, GPOs, patient-support hubs, and related pharmaceutical channel stakeholders.
Experience supporting a first market entry or launch for a publicly traded company is preferred.
Strong analytical capabilities with the ability to translate market and operational data into actionable strategies.
Executive presence, strong accountability, and the ability to make informed decisions in complex and evolving environments.
Proven ability to manage multiple priorities and projects while maintaining effective execution.
Demonstrated experience building and leading high-performing teams.
Strong interpersonal and communication skills, with the ability to coordinate effectively across multiple functions and stakeholder groups.
Highly effective, solution-oriented approach to multitasking, operational challenges, and strategic problem-solving.
Ability to establish trusted external partnerships and influence senior stakeholders.
Willingness and ability to travel 50% or more, including regular travel to Boston.
Alignment with values centered on patient impact, adaptability, momentum, transparency, and constructive candor.

Benefits

Fully remote position within the United States.
Senior executive-level opportunity supporting the commercial launch of an innovative pharmaceutical product.
Opportunity to shape trade, distribution, GPO, patient-support, and field reimbursement strategies from the ground up.
Significant influence across market access, commercial operations, supply chain, finance, legal, compliance, regulatory, and marketing functions.
Opportunity to build and lead a high-performing cross-functional organization.
Direct involvement in strategic partner relationships and complex pharmaceutical channel negotiations.
High level of strategic ownership and visibility within a growing biotech environment.
50%+ travel, including regular opportunities to collaborate in person at the Boston office.

How Jobgether Works

to ensure your application is reviewed quickly, objectively, and fairly against the role's core requirements. Our system identifies the top-fitting candidates, and this shortlist is then shared directly with the hiring company. The final decision and next steps (interviews, assessments) are managed by their internal team.

We appreciate your interest and wish you the best!

Why Apply Through Jobgether?

Data Privacy Notice:
By submitting your application, you acknowledge that Jobgether will process your personal data to evaluate your candidacy and share relevant information with the hiring employer. This processing is based on legitimate interest and pre-contractual measures under applicable data protection laws (including GDPR). You may exercise your rights (access, rectification, erasure, objection) at any time.

We may use artificial intelligence (AI) tools to support parts of the hiring process, such as reviewing applications, analyzing resumes, or assessing responses and identifying potential inconsistencies or verification signals in application materials based on available information. These tools assist our recruitment team but do not replace human judgment. Final hiring decisions are ultimately made by humans. new_jobs.description:
Job Description

As a Director of Operations you will plan, manage, and guide contracted services for multiple sites for a client or for multiple clients normally generating $2-15M+ in revenue to meet operating and financial goals, client objectives, and customer needs.

Depending on the client(s), services can include food service, facility support, custodial services, retail, lodging, transportation, and more. Our Dirctor of Operations are capable operations managers who lead a team to provide excellent service to our clients. With knowledge of the client's business, positive relationship building skills, financial savvy, and a focus on safety, our team makes a difference every day.

Job Responsibilities

The Successful Director Of Operations:

Leads a team that provides operational expertise in contracted services while providing hands-on execution management of operations.
Manages the client and community relationships at the location, continually assessing operations, and developing plans to provide optimal service and drive employee and customer satisfaction.
Builds, develops, and leads a management team and staff capable of carrying out organizational objectives.
Recommends methods, resources, and implementation for service improvement and growth based on understanding of operational needs, capabilities, & contractual obligations.
In partnership with Finance, manages a budget and assists in the design of improvements to optimize financial performance and operational productivity.
Manages compliance with all local, state and federal regulations and codes and maintains all associated records and reports.
Ensures compliance with Aramark's standards of operation including safety standards and Aramark's Business Conduct Policy at all times.

Qualifications

In order to be prepared for this leadership role, qualified candidates will possess:

Bachelor's degree level education highly preferred in an area of Food Service, Hospitality, Facilities, or Business Management.
The ability to focus on client and customer services, entrepreneurship and building and growing a strong business is essential to success in this role.
Savvy interpersonal skills to communicate effectively with clients, senior management, and Aramark support staff.
Comfortable reading, understanding, and implementing contractual requirements, including identifying opportunities within contract terms and conditions to address operational issues.
Meaningful experience in service industry, contract services, or hospitality environment.
Proven ability leading through other managers.
Experience in creating and managing a department budget, financial controls and analysis.
Experience crafting product sales strategies and implementing operational programs and initiatives.

This role may have physical demands including, but not limited to, lifting, bending, pushing, pulling and/or extended walking and standing. This role may also require uniforms and/or usage of Personal Protective Equipment (PPE).

new_jobs.title: Director of Communications & Public Engagement
new_jobs.description:
Position Overview

This position is a 1.0 FTE appointment serving the School Architecture and Design at the University of Kansas.

Working in collaboration with the Dean and the leadership team of the School, the position oversees all communications and marketing initiatives for the School and its units to translate complex students, alumni, faculty and staff achievements and impacts into clear, compelling narratives that improve student enrollment, retention, engagement and success; support advancement and fundraising; and promote reputation and community excellence.

The position is a member of the Dean’s leadership team. The position liaises with KU Marketing and Public Affairs, and KU Endowment Association on matters related to communications and public engagement. The position supervises the Graphic Designer of the School and a staff of student employees. The Position serves at the pleasure of the Dean and reports to the Dean.

Job Description

Responsibilities Related to Strategic Communications (90%)

Strategic Leadership Responsibilities

Works with the Dean and the leadership team of the School to develop and implement an integrated strategic communications plan to advance the School’s brand and increase awareness of its programs, activities, and mission. The plan will identify priority audiences, messages, channels, responsibilities, an editorial schedule, and measures of success.
Works directly and regularly with Department Chairs to understand departmental priorities, upcoming initiatives, events, accomplishments, recruitment needs, and opportunities for communication and promotion. Meets with the Chairs collectively or individually at least four times each academic year( twice per semester) to maintain consistent communication between the departments and the School’s communications efforts.
Provides editorial direction and brand management to enhance School brand and reputation.
Provides oversight of the School’s marketing and communications materials. Establishes and manages a process for review and feedback on visual communications, actively seeking input from School leadership to help ensure materials appropriately represent the School and its programs.
Develops a communications strategy for increasing the visibility of faculty research, scholarship, and creative activity across Architecture & Design, identifying opportunities to promote faculty expertise and accomplishments to academic, professional, industry, media, alumni, donor, and public audiences.

Day-to-day management responsibilities:

Maintains a clear editorial and project process for intake, prioritization, approvals, production, status updates, publication, and follow-up across web, social media, email, print, media relations, and events.
Builds and executes systematic and sustainable processes for documenting School outputs, events, lectures, faculty and student research, and activities with alumni, community and industry.
Maintains an active presence across the School and regularly engages with faculty and students to develop a strong understanding of the School’s programs, people, activities, accomplishments, and culture. Identifies stories and communications opportunities through direct engagement with the School community rather than relying solely on submitted content.
Attends key School events, Annual Board Meetings, lectures, exhibitions, reviews, student activities, and other activities as appropriate to identify and capture stories, moments, quotes, achievements, and other content for use across School communications.
Meets regularly with faculty across Architecture and Design to learn about their current and emerging research, scholarship, creative activity, publications, exhibitions, awards, grants, collaborations, and areas of expertise. Proactively identifies opportunities to translate and promote this work through School communications rather than relying solely on faculty to submit stories or requests.
Coordinates photography and other documentation of student work, faculty activities, events, exhibitions, facilities, and the everyday life of the School, working with professional photographers, student employees, faculty, and staff as appropriate.
Builds and executes systematic and sustainable processes for managing assets for public communications that strategically and creatively promote the past, present and future of the School.
Establishes a sustainable, repeatable and effective way for faculty, staff and students to submit requests, understand priorities, know who approves the work, and see what is moving forward.
Maintains the School website as a current and accurate representation of its programs, people, student work, research, activities, and accomplishments. Establishes a schedule for ongoing updates and an annual refresh of student work, photography, program information, and editorial content so that the website remains timely, relevant, and visually engaging.

Production Responsibilities

Manages the School’s websites and webpages including maintaining current content, improving navigation and usability, and ensuring information is accurate and accessible.
Manages the production of marketing and recruitment collateral materials of the School in collaboration with the Director of Recruitment and Enrollment and the Chairs, highlighting the Return on Investment (ROI) of a specific academic program through career outcomes, salary data, and alumni success; student experience; and innovation and research.
Manages the production of weekly newsletters for students and faculty in collaboration with the Director of Student Services and Success and the Chairs, highlighting weekly events and activities, policy updates, programmatic changes, and School resources to improve internal community engagement, inclusivity, and belonging.
Manages the production of the bi-monthly ArcD Newsletter highlighting student, faculty and alumni achievements and stories to improve engagement within the broader School community, including alumni, donors, and industry and community partners.
Manages the semiannual or annual publication/s of the School focusing on research, community, and economic impacts of the School for regional, national and international audiences.
Develops and produces ongoing stories and content that make faculty research, scholarship, creative activity, and expertise accessible and visible to audiences through the website, newsletters, social media, publications, media outreach, and other appropriate channels.

Public Engagement Responsibilities

Develops and promotes a unified ecosystem of public engagement for the School. Such an ecosystem will have multiple points of entry for both internal and external constituents to the creative and research output, community-engaged activities, events and workshops, services, and everyday life of the School; and will use the digital, physical, spatial and human assets of the School.
Builds relationships with faculty and students across Architecture and Design to ensure that communications reflect the breadth of the School and that emerging work, accomplishments, research, creative activity, and student experiences are identified and communicated.
Actively promotes faculty research and expertise.
Develops and stores collections and coordinates services that enhance communications and engagement activities through exhibitions, displays and other public efforts.
Promotes a positive and cooperative team environment among all stakeholder groups.
Pitches faculty experts to journalists for commentary on breaking news to elevate the unit's national profile.

Supervisory and Other Responsibilities (10%)

Supervises the Graphic Designer of the School and a staff of student employees.
Develops guidelines to distinguish the director’s strategy, priority-setting, and approval responsibilities from the designer’s creative and production responsibilities.
Establishes clear expectations and review processes for the quality and consistency of visual communications produced by the School. Actively seeks design expertise and feedback to help establish and maintain the visual direction of the School, ensuring that communications reflect the quality and standards of a School of Architecture and Design.
Develops clear expectations for staff development, workload priorities, coverage, delegation, and consistent service to the members of the School community.
Serves on committees, as needed.
Participates in and provides communications support for School activities including Board meetings, alumni events and award ceremonies, donor events, lecture series, and exhibitions.
Performs other duties in support of the mission of the School.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s Degree in Journalism, Communications, Marketing, Business Administration or a related field and five years of related experience
Previous experience with editing, writing and website maintenance
At least one year of supervisory experience
Prior work experience working with a wide range of populations, as demonstrated by application materials and work history

This position requires a formal degree in the cited discipline area(s) to ensure that candidates have advanced knowledge, analytical skills and professional competencies necessary to perform the duties of the position. The level of degree is commonly recognized as the standard qualification for similar roles in the public and private sector, ensuring that the university remains competitive with industry aligned practices, enhances collaboration with external partners, and supports the delivery of services and programs that meet professional and market-driven expectations.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with AI technologies for predictive analytics and yield modeling; personalized campaigns; and for administrative automation and document processing
Excellent computer skills and demonstrated interest and capacity in database management
Experience collaborating with different levels of leadership, including university and school leaderships as demonstrated by application materials and work history
Experience with strategic communications
Knowledge of developing surveys and analyzing data for reporting purposes
Proven experience exercising initiatives, decision-making and self-discipline
Experience in all or some of the other areas of responsibilities of the position
Demonstrated effective written communication skills as evidenced by application materials
Demonstrated organizational skills and demonstrated ability to handle multiple projects and juggle priorities

new_jobs.title: Executive Director, Trade Relations
new_jobs.description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Executive Director, Trade Relations based in United States.

This senior leadership role owns trade and patient-support strategy in preparation for the commercial launch of an innovative pharmaceutical product.

Reporting to the SVP of Market Access, you will define enterprise-wide approaches across distribution, GPOs, patient support programs, and strategic partners.

The position serves as a critical connection point between commercial strategy and operational execution, ensuring channels and partners are launch-ready.

You will work closely with Finance, Marketing, Legal, Compliance, Commercial Operations, Supply Chain, Regulatory, and Market Access teams to establish effective trade operations.

The role combines strategic planning, complex contract negotiations, organizational leadership, operational problem-solving, and performance management.

You will also establish governance frameworks that support compliant, consistent, and high-quality patient services while optimizing access and product availability.

This is a remote executive opportunity with significant external engagement and 50%+ travel, including regular travel to Boston.

Accountabilities

Lead product launch readiness by gathering, evaluating, and integrating critical trade, distribution, and patient-support requirements.
Design and execute comprehensive trade and patient-support strategies that strengthen market access and improve the overall patient experience.
Develop and implement GPO contracting strategies aligned with market access priorities and commercial objectives.
Build and lead a high-performing organization spanning trade operations, patient support, and field reimbursement.
Lead strategic negotiations with specialty distributors, specialty pharmacies, GPOs, patient hubs, and other key channel partners.
Serve as the primary subject-matter expert for trade operations, providing internal teams with relevant channel insights, guidance, and strategic direction.
Identify operational risks, inefficiencies, and opportunities, developing foundational and innovative solutions that improve efficiency, profitability, and product availability.
Monitor competitive and market dynamics to anticipate challenges, inform strategic decisions, and identify emerging opportunities.
Establish and maintain patient-support policies, business rules, governance structures, and operating frameworks that promote compliant and consistent service delivery.
Build and maintain trusted relationships with strategic external partners to strengthen collaboration and long-term value.
Ensure trade and patient-support initiatives are delivered against budgets, forecasts, operational objectives, and broader corporate performance targets.
Drive cross-functional alignment across commercial, operational, regulatory, financial, legal, and compliance stakeholders to ensure coordinated execution.

Requirements

Bachelor’s degree in a relevant field; an MBA is preferred.
12+ years of experience across pharmaceutical trade, distribution, GPOs, patient support, and strategic partner management.
Demonstrated pharmaceutical trade and patient-support experience supporting the launch of a new product.
Experience developing and implementing channel strategies in complex pharmaceutical environments.
Experience negotiating, implementing, executing, and monitoring contracts with channel partners.
Experience with specialty distributors, specialty pharmacies, GPOs, patient-support hubs, and related pharmaceutical channel stakeholders.
Experience supporting a first market entry or launch for a publicly traded company is preferred.
Strong analytical capabilities with the ability to translate market and operational data into actionable strategies.
Executive presence, strong accountability, and the ability to make informed decisions in complex and evolving environments.
Proven ability to manage multiple priorities and projects while maintaining effective execution.
Demonstrated experience building and leading high-performing teams.
Strong interpersonal and communication skills, with the ability to coordinate effectively across multiple functions and stakeholder groups.
Highly effective, solution-oriented approach to multitasking, operational challenges, and strategic problem-solving.
Ability to establish trusted external partnerships and influence senior stakeholders.
Willingness and ability to travel 50% or more, including regular travel to Boston.
Alignment with values centered on patient impact, adaptability, momentum, transparency, and constructive candor.

Benefits

Fully remote position within the United States.
Senior executive-level opportunity supporting the commercial launch of an innovative pharmaceutical product.
Opportunity to shape trade, distribution, GPO, patient-support, and field reimbursement strategies from the ground up.
Significant influence across market access, commercial operations, supply chain, finance, legal, compliance, regulatory, and marketing functions.
Opportunity to build and lead a high-performing cross-functional organization.
Direct involvement in strategic partner relationships and complex pharmaceutical channel negotiations.
High level of strategic ownership and visibility within a growing biotech environment.
50%+ travel, including regular opportunities to collaborate in person at the Boston office.
